teaser.text: Rockwell Automation sells the machinery, software and expertise that help factories make things safely and repeatedly. Its business begins with a factory investment, passes through equipment, licenses and services, and ends with money paid to suppliers and employees, with profit left over.

stock.title: Rockwell stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Rockwell stock forecast: weighted scenarios show a wide range, hinging on recovery, profitable growth and durable cash generation.
stock.opening: The weighted scenario points to a 1% loss including dividends by October 2027 and a 13% return by October 2029. It hinges on continued recovery, profitable growth and cash generation without a sharp valuation reset.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Rockwell’s business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Rockwell’s shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is $415.86 in October 2027, a 1% loss including dividends. It reaches $465.44 in October 2029, a 13% return including dividends. The forecast assigns 25% probability to the bear case and 55% to base. The bull case carries 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Rockwell?

paragraphs.text: The bear case requires customers to resume destocking, defer capacity and resist price increases while input costs rise. Operating profit weakens, the multiple contracts and the shares fall from $341.30 in October 2027 to $306.86 in October 2029. Its probability is 25% because FY2024 already produced an 8.8% sales decline, and Lifecycle Services book-to-bill was below one in Q3 FY2026.

The bull case requires modernization to broaden across semiconductors, warehouses and data centers. Higher volume, favorable mix, recurring software and productivity lift operating profit to $2,464 million by 2029, while buybacks accelerate. The shares rise from $484.73 to $629.97. Its probability is 20% because the outcome depends on several uncertain drivers working together, including software economics and the five-year $2 billion expansion.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Rockwell really make?

paragraphs.text: Rockwell generates substantial cash, but FY2025 benefited from working-capital timing. Cash from operations was $1,544 million in FY2025, compared with net income of $869 million.

Timing also helped. A $70 million pension contribution reduced cash without creating a new earnings charge, and incentive payments moved between reporting years. Subtracting $85 million of stock compensation gives an analytical “real free cash flow” figure, because stock pay can dilute owners.

blocks.heading: How much does Rockwell pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: Dividend growth follows the company’s record but respects its discretion. The base dividend rises from $5.80 to $6.08 and then $6.36, close to the recent 5% annual pace. The bear case holds the current $5.52 run-rate unchanged. The bull case reaches $6.00, then $6.48 and $6.96 on stronger cash generation. The latest quarterly rate was $1.38, and annual dividends rose from $4.28 in FY2021 to $5.24 in FY2025.

blocks.heading: Is Rockwell’s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: After $186 million of capital spending, FY2025 free cash flow was $1,358 million. Capital spending supports the operating asset base, while much engineering and development spending passes through the income statement. Rockwell does not separate maintenance spending from growth spending, so all free cash flow is not automatically distributable.

blocks.heading: What is Rockwell’s dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: At $426.23 a share on October 18, 2026, Rockwell’s equity value was $47,332.28 million. Enterprise value, which adds debt and subtracts cash to approximate the value of the operating business, was $50,111.28 million. The $2,779 million difference represents the implied net-debt adjustment. Think of a house: its full value belongs partly to the lender, while the owner receives only the remaining equity.

Cash returns set the starting hurdle. Free-cash-flow yield was 2.9%, while the extra deduction behind “real” free cash flow produced 2.7%. The dividend yield was 1.3%. Against a 5.09% US 10-year Treasury yield on October 16, 2026, Rockwell needs growth to justify its premium.

earnings.title: Rockwell earnings: guidance and what to watch
earnings.meta_description: Rockwell expects results on November 5, 2026; guidance calls for reported sales growth, adjusted EPS, and free cash flow.
earnings.opening: Rockwell's next results are expected on November 5, 2026. Watch whether pricing keeps pace with component inflation.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers how Rockwell's business, rivals, management, and risks shape its outlook.

blocks.heading: What has Rockwell guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Guidance is management’s forecast, not a guarantee. Rockwell’s latest forecast, issued August 4, 2026, covers the year ended September 30, 2026. It calls for reported sales of approximately $9,000 million and reported and organic sales growth of 7.5%–9.5%. It also calls for adjusted EPS of $13.00–$13.30. Adjusted EPS removes specified items, such as acquisition-related amortization, so it helps compare operations but is not the same as accounting profit.

blocks.heading: Has Rockwell kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Other outcomes show that the system can reduce rewards. Moret received no annual incentive for fiscal 2024. The performance-share cycle covering 2023–2025 paid 70% of target, meaning executives received roughly seventy shares for every one hundred target shares under the plan’s rules. Rockwell also reached its savings goal early, although savings must persist without weakening customer support.

blocks.heading: What is Rockwell's eight-quarter revenue and profit trend?

paragraphs.text: All three earlier FY2026 quarters exceeded their comparable FY2025 quarters. But June gross margin was below March’s 50.2%, despite higher sequential sales. Year-over-year recovery and quarter-to-quarter momentum are different questions.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Rockwell's next results?

paragraphs.text: The nearest checkpoint is November 5, 2026, an estimated date for the next earnings release. Rockwell had not issued FY27 guidance on its Q3 call, so investors will compare analysts’ expectations with management’s first commitment on sales, margins, capital spending, and cash flow. The annual investor meeting on November 18, 2026, should provide another explanation of the program and its expected returns.

Finally, watch whether pricing keeps pace with component inflation. Management expected higher memory costs to pressure Software & Control’s fourth-quarter margin. The strongest outlook would combine sustained demand, cash arriving as forecast, and investment benefits appearing without increasingly heavy borrowing.
